doc.title: Jones Hank — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Savoy sessions in Rudy Van Gelder's Hackensack home
summary: The interviewer lists 1946-47 Savoy dates with Getz, Dizzy Gillespie and J.J. Johnson; Jones says most were in Van Gelder's home.

bands.name: Ray Brown and the Be Bop Boys

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: Around this time, it is 1946, you started an association with Savoy Records. I think the first recording is with Stan Getz. I think it was with Stan Getz, Curly Russell, and Max.
Then in 1947, Ray Brown and the Be bop boys is what I have. Dizzy, Dave Burns, John Brown, James Moody, Milt Jackson, Hank Jones…
I don't know how they got all those people in Rudy Van Gelder’s studio

Right. 12/24/1947, JJ Johnson’s bebop quintet. These sessions would come with great rapidity. I mean when I would go through, like, one day it is this band, it's Eddie Bird… It is almost like you lived in that Savoy Studio for a bit.

For quite a while I did. I did a lot of work out there. But, that was in his home, when he lived in Hackensack. He moved into a studio on 9W near Fort Lee. No, it was Inglewood Cliffs rather. That was a much larger studio. But, most of that early stuff, that Savoy stuff took place in Rudy's home in Hackensack. In fact, I don't think we did any Savoy studio records in his studio on 9W. I think, the date that I did with Cannonball Adderley, it might have been with Bluenote. That was something else.
